judge.label: LLM rubric score, fresh-context judge, self-assessed — not human QA.
judge.independence_caveat: This judge is a different model family and a fresh context: it saw only the judge prompt, the rubric and the lesson. It did not direct the project and did not author anything in it. It is still a language model scoring a language model's output, so the label applies: not human QA.

notes.knowledge_check: Distractors are plausible and drawn from real misconceptions (staying silent, asking vague questions). Feedback is diagnostic. One distractor in KC-02 ('Suggesting changes') is slightly less plausible than the others but still reasonable for an over-eager new starter.

verdict_notes: A strong, well-aligned lesson with excellent bilingual quality and authentic scenarios. The worked example and scenario both show realistic friction and model the desired behavior clearly. All criteria score well above the floor.
